## Equations
### ZNE001 — Polynomial expansion under uniform physical-noise amplification

*Shows that an FTQC observable remains a polynomial in a common physical-error scale even with measurements, feedback, post-selection, and decoding.*

$$
\langle O\rangle(r)=\langle O\rangle_{\mathrm{ideal}}+\sum_{k=1}^{N}a_k r^k
$$

status: `verified` · source: main_text: Results, polynomial form immediately before Fig. 1; supplement: Supplementary Eqs. (11)--(18)

Numerical form:

```
Evaluate the independently specified noise model at explicit scale factors r; do not fit or sample source-figure pixels.
```

Code: `src/qem_models.py::zne_weights`


### ZNE002 — Distance-aware polynomial extrapolation

*Cancels the first K surviving logical-error powers, beginning at the code-corrected order m.*

$$
m=\lceil d/2\rceil,\quad V_{i0}=1,\quad V_{ij}=r_i^{m+j-1}\ (j>0),\quad b_k=(V^{-1})_{0k},\quad \langle O\rangle_{\mathrm{em}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K}b_k\langle O\rangle(r_k)
$$

status: `verified` · derived from: `ZNE001` · source: main_methods: Methods Eqs. (3)--(4); main_results: Fitting basis beginning at ceil(d/2)

Numerical form:

```
Build V from the declared r values and solve V.T * b = e0; never use an image-derived fit.
```

Code: `src/qem_models.py::zne_weights`, `src/qem_models.py::zne_estimate`


### ZNE003 — Bias and optimally allocated sampling overhead

*Separates accuracy improvement from the sampling cost for a Pauli observable.*

$$
\delta=|\langle O\rangle_{\mathrm{em}}-\langle O\rangle_{\mathrm{ideal}}|,\quad N_k=\frac{|b_k|}{B}N_{\mathrm{tot}},\quad \eta=\frac{B\sum_k|b_k|[1-\langle O\rangle(r_k)^2]}{1-\langle O\rangle(r_0)^2},\quad B=\sum_k|b_k|
$$

status: `verified` · derived from: `ZNE002` · source: main_text: Main Eqs. (1)--(2); main_methods: Methods variance and shot-allocation paragraph

Numerical form:

```
Use analytic expectation values O(r_k), the same total-shot convention, and return infinity only when the raw Pauli variance is exactly zero.
```

Code: `src/qem_models.py::zne_metrics`


### FB001 — Exact feedback and post-selection response of Main Fig. 2

*Gives the injection-only numerical curves without reading the paper plot or author arrays.*

$$
q=2rp/3,\quad \langle Z_0\rangle_{\mathrm{raw}}=\cos\theta_0(1-2q),\quad P_{\mathrm{acc}}=(1-q)^2+q^2,\quad \langle Z_0\rangle_{\mathrm{corr}}=\cos\theta_0\frac{1-2q}{1-2q+2q^2}
$$

status: `reconstructed` · derived from: `ZNE001` · source: main_text: Main Fig. 2 and the feedback parity-check experiment; supplement: Supplementary Note 3, Pauli insertion probabilities

Numerical form:

```
For each data qubit X/Y contributes a classical Z-basis flip with probability q. Q3 accepts e2=e4; Q1 feedback leaves residual flip e2.
```

Code: `src/qem_models.py::feedback_expectation`, `src/qem_models.py::feedback_expectation_enumerated`


### REP001 — Repetition-code logical failure and multi-round composition

*Provides a closed-form, independently checkable model of the distance and round scaling emphasized by the paper.*

$$
q=2rp/3,\quad P_L(d,q)=\sum_{j=\lceil d/2\rceil}^{d}{d\choose j}q^j(1-q)^{d-j},\quad \langle Z_L\rangle_{\mathrm{corr}}=[1-2P_L(d,q)]^{M+1},\quad \langle Z_L\rangle_{\mathrm{raw}}=(1-2q)^{M+1}
$$

status: `reconstructed` · derived from: `ZNE001` · source: main_text: Main Fig. 3 repetition-code protocol; supplement: Supplementary Table 3 and Note 4

Numerical form:

```
Evaluate the binomial tail with integer arithmetic/scipy-free summation; optionally compose disclosed median gate/readout flips as a separate, labelled calibration model.
```

Code: `src/qem_models.py::repetition_logical_failure`, `src/qem_models.py::repetition_expectation`


### SURF001 — Exact distance-3 rotated-surface-code Pauli channel

*Enumerates all 4^9 physical Pauli errors, applies an independently reconstructed minimum-weight CSS decoder, and returns the logical I/X/Y/Z channel.*

$$
P_{\ell}(p)=\sum_{E\in\mathcal P_9}(1-p)^{9-w(E)}(p/3)^{w(E)}\,\mathbf 1\{L[D(s(E))E]=\ell\},\quad p_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac34\left[1-\prod_j(1-4p_j/3)\right]
$$

status: `reconstructed` · derived from: `ZNE001` · source: main_text: Main Fig. 4 and logical operators XL=X_D1 X_D4 X_D7, ZL=Z_D3 Z_D4 Z_D5; supplement: Supplementary Fig. 6 and Note 4 numerical-simulation paragraph

Numerical form:

```
Pre-enumerate each Pauli pattern's weight and decoded logical class, then evaluate its probability polynomial for each effective depolarizing rate.
```

Code: `src/surface_code.py::logical_channel`, `src/surface_code.py::validate_code`


### MEM001 — Bravyi--Vargo logical-memory fit used by Supplementary Fig. 9

*Reproduces the paper's large-scale surface-code memory estimate and its distance-aware ZNE calculation.*

$$
r_d=(d+1)/4,\quad P_L(p,d)=\exp[-\alpha(p)(r_d-2)+4\ln p+x(p)],\quad -\alpha(p)=c+2\ln p+\ln(1+y(p)),\quad \langle O\rangle(r)=[1-2P_L(rp,d)]^N
$$

status: `verified` · derived from: `ZNE002`, `ZNE003` · source: supplement: Supplementary Fig. 9 and surrounding text; primary_reference: Bravyi and Vargo, Phys. Rev. A 88, 062308 (2013), Eqs. (2)--(3), Table I

Numerical form:

```
Use noisy-syndrome path coefficients x=(9.88,1170,-76400), c=7.52, y=(880,4690,6.04e6); use r_d=(d+1)/4 for d=7,11,15.
```

Code: `src/qem_models.py::bravyi_vargo_path_error`, `src/qem_models.py::logical_memory_expectation`
